function: CSI feedback: the UE compresses the CSI with a random linear projection and a CNN decoder at the BS reconstructs it; Learngene eases deployment (pp. 3-4).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM, 32-antenna ULA at BS, single-antenna UE, 512 subcarriers, 2.6 GHz, 20 MHz, no RIS (p. 11, Table III).
method: CNN decoder, supervised MSE training; Learngene layers from a collective model trained on 90 scenes initialize a lighter individual model, fine-tuned with L2 regularization (pp. 6-9, 11).
data_channel: Wireless AI Research Dataset, a public ray-tracing tool on maps of 40+ cities; 100 scenarios, 10,000 single-antenna UEs each; split 0.85/0.10/0.05 (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: Collective model trained on 90 scenarios; individual model fine-tuned on a scenario unseen by it (10 held-out tasks); CR 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Train-from-scratch (same network, random initialization) and classic pretrain-finetune transfer learning (refs. [26], [27], [29]); no non-learned baseline (p. 12).
metrics: NMSE in dB, epochs to converge, training samples needed, transmitted parameters (communication cost), model disclosure (p. 10, Table II; Figs. 9-10).
complexity: FLOPs and parameters of collective, individual and Learngene networks: individual 7.59e8 FLOPs, 7.41e5 params; Learngene unit 4.53e8, 4.42e5 (p. 12, Table V).
openness: Own code and data not released; uses the public Wireless AI Research Dataset, https://www.mobileaidataset.com/ (ref. [51], p. 16).
q1_support: p. 10: "a publicly available and novel software called the Wireless AI Research Dataset"; the CSI is ray-traced on real city maps ("simulated using ray-tracing techniques").
q2_support: p. 11: "the remaining 10 tasks tested the adaptability of the individual model to new tasks" (pretrained on 90 scenes, then fine-tuned on a scenario not accessible to the collective model, Table IV).
q3_support: p. 12: "against two benchmarks: train-from-scratch and transfer learning"; both are learned networks and no non-learned method (compressed sensing, codebook) is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: Table V has "FLOPs" and "Params" columns: individual model 7.59e8 and 7.41e5, Learngene unit 4.53e8 and 4.42e5 (Group 1).
q5_support: p. 10: "a publicly available and novel software called the Wireless AI Research Dataset [51]"; p. 16: ref. [51] gives "https://www.mobileaidataset.com/".
notes: Area 2: the learned method is CSI compression and reconstruction. The BS has 32 antennas (p. 11, Table III), so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. q1 and q5 rest on the Wireless AI Research Dataset (CAICT, ref. [51]), a public ray-tracing channel tool on real city maps, which is not one of the named 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO models: the reviewer should confirm. q3 is 0 because the only baselines are train-from-scratch and transfer learning (p. 12), which use the same CNN as the proposed method trained in another way, and no non-learned baseline appears in Section IV, Table II or Table VI. The FLOPs and parameter counts of q4 are in Table V (p. 12), whose body is not in the extracted text and was read on the page image. No code release is stated.
